thread_title: S. leucophylla 'neat lip' Baldwin Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla 'neat lip' Baldwin Co, AL

posts.body_html:
Rocket Scientist: yo M-Dubz in the hiznouse...Son...... how did you come up with that name?
MW:I wasn't aware that professional scientists speak such archaic, 1990's slang. Nevertheless, I think the name was derived from the following formula: F(x)+delta X -F(x)/delta x elementary, Doc, it's elementary.
Rocket Scientist: Ummm, the math doesn't add up, and that equation is non sequitur, given that you provided a random math equation that has nothing to do with my question.
MW: uuuuuuh (with a dumb, stupor-like tone), it doesn't take a rocket scientist to figure out the name, duuuude. Just look at the lips, maaaan!

Long story short, a rocket scientist isn't required to figure out how the name of this clone came to be! However, it might take a rocket scientist to figure out whether or not we should classify this as an alba or not. It probably is, but since it's so dang hard to "alba up" I'll just call it a regular leuco for now. Maybe that'll change if it whitens up in the interior consistently in the years to come.

I mean, maybe I shoulda called this thing pointy lip, cuz look at how pointy that thing is! The clone is well into circulation, so I don't want to cause confusion, so the old name stays. Pics taken 10/18/20:


Dang, that is looking alba-ey:
